description: Returns a published government fee and its effective date. For US (the default), the general filing fee for a USCIS form and filing method. I-129, I-131, and I-907 have no general filing fee: pass category. For I-131, the label this tool uses: a short name of the Appendix B heading, a colon, and the item selector, such as "Reentry Permit: Part 1., Item Number 1." For I-129 and I-907, the category argument says how to name the classification. US covers I-90, I-130, I-140, I-485, I-539, I-765, and N-400, paper and online, and I-129, I-131, and I-907 by category; only some G-1055 categories are covered, and an uncovered one returns no fee. An I-129 amount is the filing fee G-1055 lists for that row. Fees G-1055 lists apart from it are not in the amount. An I-907 amount is the premium processing fee only, not the fee for the form it accompanies. Any other form returns not_found. For GB, the fee for a published Home Office fee category; pass the section heading as category when the name appears in more than one section. For AU, a visa application charge component that Migration Regulations 1994, Schedule 1 states for a visa subclass, from the item's table for any other applicant or its only charge table. Pass the subclass as form, such as "189", and the component as category, such as "Base application charge"; category is required when the subclass has more than one component. 500 and 590 are subclasses whose charge Schedule 1 states in item 1222. Other amounts apply to some applicants; notes names the item and compilation. amount_cents is in the minor unit of currency. filing is "unspecified" when the source states no filing channel. It does not say which fee applies to a case. For a USCIS form's current edition, use check_form_edition. Requires sign-in at https://immigrationlayer.com/login and an active plan. Without a plan it returns subscription_required. Limit: 30 calls per minute per account, shared by all paid tools, then rate_limited. Not legal advice. Sources: for US, the USCIS fee schedule (Form G-1055), the 2024 USCIS fee rule (89 FR 6194), and, for I-907, the 2026 premium processing fee rule (91 FR 1059); for GB, the Home Office visa regulations revised table on gov.uk, used under the Open Government Licence v3.0; for AU, Migration Regulations 1994, Schedule 1. Australian charges are based on content from the Federal Register of Legislation, CC BY 4.0.

category.description: For US I-131, a short name of the Appendix B heading, a colon, and the item selector, such as "Reentry Permit: Part 1., Item Number 1." For US I-129, the classification label exactly as G-1055 Appendix A prints it, such as "If you are filing H-1B or H-1B1 petitions."; for a small employer row, that label, a space, and "If you are filing as a Small Employer or Nonprofit." For US I-907, the classification label exactly as G-1055 prints it, such as "H-2B or R nonimmigrant classification". Required for I-129, I-131, and I-907. For GB, the published section heading. Required when the fee category name appears in more than one section. For AU, the charge component exactly as the item states it, such as "Base application charge"; required when the subclass has more than one.

filing.description: How the form is filed: "paper" (mailed) or "online" (USCIS online account). Required for US. Ignored for GB and AU.

form.description: For US, the USCIS form number exactly as USCIS writes it, e.g. "I-765"; "i765" and "I765" do not match. For GB, the published Home Office fee category name. For AU, the three-digit visa subclass, such as "500".

amount_cents.description: Fee in the minor unit of currency; 47000 with USD is $470.00.

attribution.description: Licence attribution for the source data. Present for AU, absent for US and GB.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for amount_cents, e.g. "USD" or "GBP".

effective_date.description: Date this fee took effect, YYYY-MM-DD

notes.description: Where the source states the charge and what can change it. Present for AU, absent for US and GB.
